claims.statement: Photovoltaic panels are expressly within the WEEE framework, including producer-financing and collection obligations for covered panels.
Poland's BDO system provides registry, waste-record, reporting, and confirmation modules under the Waste Act.

contrary_evidence: Existing producer-responsibility schemes and recyclers may already satisfy installer needs, while reuse claims cannot be used to evade waste rules.

economics.acquisition_route: Embed digital take-back selection in installer job closeout and acquire installers through wholesalers and the family company
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Enroll 150 installers by year 3 (unvalidated), process national multi-stream returns by year 6 (unvalidated), and build founder equity above PLN 5 million by year 8 (unvalidated)
economics.founder_time: 12-18 hours per week during validation (unvalidated), with transport outsourced
economics.gross_margin_basis: Route aggregation, compliance records, and buyer matching while licensed partners handle regulated treatment; 30-50% gross margin (unvalidated)
economics.pricing: PLN 200-500 pickup administration per job (unvalidated), PLN 150-400 installer subscription per month (unvalidated), plus remarketing spread (unvalidated)
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual installer subscriptions (unvalidated) and repeat flows on every replacement job

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Route density, provenance records, and repeat installer contracts improve recovery economics and buyer trust
fingerprint.customer: Renewable installers, equipment producers, asset owners, reuse buyers, and licensed recyclers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Installer workflow integrations and electrical-wholesaler partnerships
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Contracted take-back, condition evidence, chain of custody, and matched lawful destination
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Installer or producer pays when a return is documented and collected; buyer pays when reusable inventory transfers
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A replacement or repowering job creates equipment whose title, condition, and lawful destination must be resolved

founder_fit: Directly leverages the family installer channel.
Traceability and routing suit quantitative automation.
Licensed partners can own manual logistics.
risks: Misclassification or undocumented transport creates regulatory exposure.
Early PV waste volumes may be too sparse for route economics.
The stated PLN 150000 startup capital requirement is unvalidated.

structure.commercial_archetype: Reverse-logistics and recommerce network with chain-of-custody services
structure.control_point: Installer take-back contracts and asset-level provenance from removal decision to authorized destination
structure.critical_dependency: Correct waste-versus-product classification, BDO duties, licensed logistics partners, and sufficient recovered value per route

thesis: Embed signed take-back instructions into installer replacement jobs so panels, inverters, cable, and mounting hardware flow to documented reuse, parts harvesting, or licensed WEEE treatment. Start as a registered broker coordinating licensed carriers and processors, taking physical custody only after securing required permissions; earn compliance, collection, and remarketing revenue from a traceable national return network.
title: PV Loop Title and Provenance Network
uncertainties: What share of removed modules is lawfully reusable after testing?
Can producer schemes contract a specialist installer-facing collection layer?
